title.narrative: Supporting displaced families and the host community with food baskets in Tal Tamr and its rural

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to distribute food baskets to the displaced individuals from Ras al-Ain city as well as to the host community in Tal Tamr and its surrounding areas. The urgent need for food assistance is underscored by the near-total cessation of food basket distributions in Tal Tamr and its countryside. The displaced population from Ras al-Ain has endured significant hardships for over four years, following their second displacement on September 10, 2019. Throughout these challenging years, marked by a persistent siege, skyrocketing food prices, and a drastic decline in the value of the Syrian currency against the dollar, the challenges facing displaced individuals have intensified across all sectors, particularly in health, food security, and other essential needs. The response from humanitarian organizations has lagged, particularly in the food sector, which ceased distributions at the end of 2023, impacting over 3,500 families. Although some distribution resumed in mid-2024, it remains inadequate, with only 500 families receiving assistance.ltbrgtThis situation is critical, as access to food is vital for survival. The goal of this food supply initiative is not only to alleviate hunger but also to save lives during these dire times. ltbrgtGiven these circumstances, it is essential to enhance our outreach and support mechanisms. We must leverage partnerships with local organizations, engage community leaders, and expand our donor base to secure the necessary resources. Furthermore, incorporating food support—such as fortified foods and awareness programs on dietary diversity—would be invaluable in addressing both immediate needs and long-term health outcomes for displaced families. And that [the association, through its ability and previous experience in reaching all areas (Tal Tar and its rural ) freely to all those affected in all areas and rural villages affiliated with the city of Tal Tamr.ltbrgtThe distribution of food baskets will help poor families, immigrants, people with special needs and vulnerable groups to overcome the difficulties of life and maintain their dignity and strengthen and support their steadfastness and stability. The association will work to focus on targeting age groups (men - women - children - girls - people with special needs - the elderly).lt/pgtltpgtGeneral objective:ltbrgt1485 families of Ras al-Ain IDPs and the host community will be targeted, where 11880 baskets will be distributed during the project period, 1485 families will receive 8 times during the project period.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTargeting MechanismltbrgtTargeting CriterialtbrgtBeneficiaries will be selected by forming committees from the targeted local community and from the association's volunteers. Forms will be filled out to identify the targeted families as follows:ltbrgtAll targeted persons must be from food-insecure families who are eligible for the food basket, with priority given to:ltbrgt Families headed by womenltbrgt Families with disabilitiesltbrgt Families with patientsltbrgt Elderly peopleltbrgt Childrenltbrgt Description of the beneficiary targeting mechanism:ltbrgto Initial registration of beneficiariesltbrgto Verification visits: Continuous by distribution officials and the distribution teamltbrgto Selection Criteria:ltbrgt Extent of damage to affected familiesltbrgt Number of family membersltbrgt Disability cases in the familyltbrgt Children in the familyltbrgt Families headed by a womanltbrgt Sources of livelihood for the familyltbrgt The elderly and disabled in the familyltbrgt Diseases, disabilities and health status in the familyltbrgtlt/pgt
